body: Good afternoon! Very exciting to see so many PR being opened for the Gridmap! I tested this fix and I can confirm that it works as expected with CenterX = CenterZ = false, and CenterY being either true of false, when: - selecting and using move operation - selecting and using duplicate operation - selecting and delete operation However, here are the situations where there is an unexpected behaviour: - selecting and using the fill operation: as we are now including the edges, we should also fill the top and right edges: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/540d5b66-7020-4ca0-84c8-575f321217e4 - move/duplicate with rotation: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/931317a0-431a-474f-bd55-407b97bd58b8 Also, I think we should consider having a toggle check box: "include edges" so that the user can decide whether to select with the edges or not. I am just thinking that such a checkbox would be more intuitive than having to select the following to only affect the floor tiles: Such a checkbox would be a nice fit for the tool setting panel suggested here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11206 and should probably be part of another PR.

> selecting and using the fill operation: as we are now including the edges, we should also fill the top and right edges The problem with adding the expanding to filling is that we end up with stuff like this:

> move/duplicate with rotation This is its own individual problem, that will need to be address by its own PR. > Also, I think we should consider having a toggle check box: "include edges" so that the user can decide whether to select with the edges or not. I am just thinking that such a checkbox would be more intuitive than having to select the following to only affect the floor tiles So the selection is grabbing unwanted tiles, like I said this approach would? And now we would have to throw in an option to disable this behavior in an checkbox that a lot of people will possibly miss.

> So the selection is grabbing unwanted tiles, like I said this approach would? 

Not exactly. What we have now is actually correct and includes all edges. While before we had a uncorrect Frankenstein mix that included the left and bottom edges and excluded the right and top edges. I am now suggesting that we could add another correct option that excludes all edges. I can write another proposal for that. 

> The problem with adding the expanding to filling is that we end up with stuff like this

I am not sure what I am looking at? What problem are you experiencing?

> Not exactly. What we have now is actually correct and includes all edges. While before we had a uncorrect Frankenstein mix that included the left and bottom edges and excluded the right and top edges. I am now suggesting that we could add another correct option that excludes all edges. I can write another proposal for that.

You did not address the problem of adding an option that would be tucked away with no clear discoverability, for a workflow that some would consider what is expected.

> I am not sure what I am looking at? What problem are you experiencing?

The fill expanding to all directions where the grid is not centered, including above. Resulting in the blocks intersecting one another.

> You did not address the problem of adding an option that would be tucked away with no clear discoverability, for a workflow that some would consider what is expected.

I suggested that this is a good candidate to appear in a tool setting panel, which would always be on screen when selecting a tool, for discoverability and practicality. See https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11206.

When working with assets aligned on edges/intersections (center x = center y = center z = false), it is probably best to have the option to include or exclude edges. We can survive with 1 of the option, but it is nicer to have both.

> The fill expanding to all directions where the grid is not centered, including above. Resulting in the blocks intersecting one another.

Can you try with a pillar as in my example above? If you are using my starter kit, the grid cells are 1x1m while the cube is 2x2m. Hence to use the filling tool will create overlapping cubes.

> When working with assets aligned on edges/intersections (center x = center y = center z = false), it is probably best to have the option to include or exclude edges. We can survive with 1 of the option, but it is nicer to have both.

I see that, but those changes are starting to feel arbitrary to a specific workflow. My fear is that if those changes pile up, they will start breaking workflows that are different from this.

> Can you try with a pillar as in my example above? If you are using my starter kit, the grid cells are 1x1m while the cube is 2x2m. Hence to use the filling tool will create overlapping cubes.

I'm aware what is causing it. What I'm point out is that this will be perceived as odd to the user, since they're selecting from a specific grid floor, but also filling the one above it.

> I see that, but those changes are starting to feel arbitrary to a specific workflow. My fear is that if those changes pile up, they will start breaking workflows that are different from this.

I agree that this is important not to break the other workflows. These changes don’t modify the selection behaviour for people working with center x = center y = center z = true though, so it should not break their workflow. 

> I'm aware what is causing it. What I'm point out is that this will be perceived as odd to the user, since they're selecting from a specific grid floor, but also filling the one above it.

oOoh, I see what you mean now! A selection of 1 unit high would include the top and bottom planes, which creates 2 layers of items when we click on the Fill operation.

Until now, I kept speaking about including or excluding edges, but in fact, I should have said “planes”.

I think this conversation shows that the on grip snap (center x = center y = center z = false) workflow is not really well supported in Godot and needs some thoughts. It is in fact more complicated to do it well than the on cell snap workflow (center x = center y = center z = true).
